name: Rice (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Rice (Oryza sativa) [Cereals and cereal products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, DUKE, PHENOL EXPLORER, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy source is STARCH (~78 g/100g, amylose+amylopectin) accessed via amylolysis to maltose/glucose; free sugars are trivial (0.12 g/100g, mostly sucrose). Rice is NOT an organic-acid-rich food: the one notable organic acid is phytic acid (~150 mg/100g), with citric/malic only trace and largely lost to milling. Values are for raw, unenriched, milled white long-grain rice (USDA FDC 169756); enriched rice would carry substantially higher B1/B3/folate/iron. Confidence high for USDA
curation_added: starch (78 g/100g) made explicit as THE dominant fermentable carbon source
phytic acid (~150 mg/100g) — the dominant organic acid/phosphate store, absent from FooDB profile
quantitative fatty-acid profile (palmitic, oleic, linoleic, alpha-linolenic, stearic)
quantitative mineral panel (P, K, Mg, Ca, Na, Fe, Zn, Mn, Cu, Se)
quantitative vitamin panel (B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, folate, E, K, choline)
citric and malic acid flagged as present-but-minor (decline with milling)

curation_removed.name: Arsenate
curation_removed.reason: Toxic metalloid contaminant (rice accumulates inorganic arsenic from paddy soil/water); a food-safety concern, not a growth nutrient.

curation_removed.name: Cholesterol
curation_removed.reason: Animal sterol, biologically implausible in a plant/cereal food; FooDB predicted-not-measured entry.

curation_removed.name: Fe2+ mitochondria
curation_removed.reason: FooDB compartment/oxidation-state duplicate of iron; consolidated into the single 'iron' component (0.8 mg/100g).

curation_removed.name: Iron (Fe3+)
curation_removed.reason: Duplicate oxidation-state entry of the same iron nutrient; consolidated into 'iron'.

curation_removed.name: Co2+
curation_removed.reason: Cobalt: ultratrace generic-element padding, not quantified/nutritionally meaningful in milled rice.

curation_removed.name: Nickel
curation_removed.reason: Ultratrace generic-element padding, not a meaningful rice growth nutrient.

curation_removed.name: Iodine c
curation_removed.reason: Ultratrace; not a meaningful/quantified nutrient of rice.

curation_removed.name: Fluoride
curation_removed.reason: Ultratrace/soil-water dependent, not a meaningful rice growth nutrient.

curation_removed.name: Molybdate
curation_removed.reason: Ultratrace generic-element padding, not quantified for milled rice.

composition_provenance.definition: sourced = the cited source states this component; derived = the pipeline supplied it. Classification table: tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv.

components.name: starch
components.evidence_source: USDA FDC 169756 (Rice, white, long-grain, regular, raw, unenriched); computed as total carbohydrate 80 g minus free sugars 0.12 g minus fibre ~0.5 g

components.name: sucrose
components.evidence_source: Perez & Juliano 1978 (milled rice, sucrose is the principal free sugar); USDA FDC 169756 total sugars 0.12 g

components.name: citric acid
components.evidence_source: Heinemann et al., processing-of-rice composition literature (organic acids decline with milling)

components.name: glycine betaine
components.evidence_source: FooDB FOOD00125; rice is a known glycine-betaine accumulator

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
